summary: Qatar’s pledges combine agricultural self-sufficiency, large-scale tree planting, and broad resilience planning. Under agriculture, it plans to reach 70% self-sufficiency in greenhouse-grown vegetables under hot conditions, supported by hydroponic greenhouses, programs, and subsidies, alongside broader efforts involving vegetables, red meat, fish, and groundwater-dependent feed production. Restoration centers on two tree initiatives: one million trees under the Plant One Million Tree Initiative, launched in 2019 and completed in 2022, and a subsequent ten-million-tree initiative launched in 2022. These efforts are notable in a landscape where forest covers only 3 km² (reported as 0.0%) and bare area occupies 91.9% of the country; the tree targets are counts, so they cannot be translated directly into hectares. A cross-cutting adaptation aim also seeks to strengthen resilience in six sectors.
